source_text: Vide ergo, utrum adhuc dubium vel tibi debeat esse, quod dicimus innocentes videlicet ante propriae voluntatis usum, rude opus Dei, non peccasse in Adam, quando Apostolo teste etiam de iniquis, qui in similitudine praevaricationis Adae non deliquerint, plurimi esse doceantur.
pass_a_gloss: See therefore whether it ought still to be doubtful even to you, what we say, namely that innocents before the use of proper will, a rude work of God, did not sin in Adam, when with the Apostle as witness even of the iniquitous, who have not offended in the likeness of Adam's transgression, very many are taught to be.

lemmas.lexica: LS praevaricatio; Blaise Adam's transgression as example
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: See, then, whether even you should still doubt what we say: that the innocent, God’s fresh handiwork before the exercise of their own will, did not sin in Adam. For even among the wicked, the apostle testifies that there are many who did not sin in the likeness of Adam’s transgression (Romans 5:14).

choices.why: Adam's act of crossing the command; Julian's example of sin, not a transmitted nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
